findings.passage: "There has been a growing concern about election security in recent years, and it is our role to ensure that our voter identification process is secure and accurate," Doriot said. findings.note: Quote in a Senate caucus release issued in his name. He explains why his bill would stop student IDs from counting as voter ID.

He lists two laws he supported: HEA 1334 (2023), which bars sending an absentee ballot application unless the person or a family member requested it, and HEA 1264 (2024), which gives clerks tools to find registered voters who may be ineligible or have inaccurate records. The list text is on the page as linked bullets; the descriptions are on the page.

Senate Bill 10, authored by Doriot. Per his release: bans student IDs as voter ID; requires voter-list maintenance at least twice a year; has county offices verify non-active voters; has the Election Division ask other states to join the Indiana Data Enhancement Association. It passed the Senate Committee on Elections that day and moved to the full Senate. Final outcome not confirmed (state bill page was blocked).

findings.passage: "It's important to ensure Indiana's voting system is secure and accurate for Hoosier voters," Doriot said.
findings.note: Quote in a Senate caucus release on the ceremonial signing of his bill banning ranked choice voting. Related election-integrity item, not about ID.

Senate Enrolled Act 12, authored by Doriot, prohibits ranked choice voting in any state or local election; ceremonially signed by the governor on this date. Related election-integrity item, not about ID.

In 2025, I authored a bill to strengthen Indiana's voter ID law by prohibiting student IDs issued by state colleges or universities from being recognized as an ID to vote, since college IDs are less secure than other forms of identification and standards vary from school to school.
findings.note: In a constituent update on the Senate caucus site, he says he authored a 2025 bill to bar state college and university student IDs as voter ID, and describes Indiana's photo ID requirement as a security measure. The page shows only a 2026 copyright, so the exact date is unknown.

findings.passage: I also supported laws: Preventing a state agency or a local government unit from sending an absentee ballot application to an individual unless the application was requested by that individual or a member of their family; and Providing county clerks and election offices with more tools to help identify registered voters who may be ineligible, or hold inaccurate records, and helping clerks take steps to update, confirm or repeal voter registrations.
findings.note: Same update: he lists two other election laws he supported, one limiting unrequested absentee ballot applications and one giving clerks tools to check voter-roll eligibility.

findings.passage: I also authored a bill that ensures Indiana's elections are secure and accurate by prohibiting the use of student IDs as a form of voter identification and requires improved voter list maintenance.
findings.note: Session-end statement issued in his name: he says he authored a bill that bars student IDs as voter ID and requires better voter list maintenance.

A news report names him as author of Senate Bill 10 (2025), which bars student IDs as valid voter ID and adds duties for local election offices. Senators voted on Monday, Jan. 27 to move it. The report says he argued student ID cards were not subject to the same rigor as driver's licenses, and that he said the BMV registration question netted non-citizens as well as unregistered voters. The report is a news page, not the legislature's own page.
